sections: stop sleeping. Mia wakes up early.
get up · /ɡɛt ʌp/ · verb · Phrase · New
get out of bed. Do you get up at seven?
to extend your arms, legs, or body to make them longer or less stiff. I stretch my arms after getting up.
sleep in · /ˌslip ˈɪn/ · verb phrase · Phrase · New
to stay asleep later than usual. I sleep in on my day off.
to do something or go somewhere very quickly. Do not rush. We have time.

articulation.label: wake
articulation.alt: wake: /w/ → /eɪ/ → /k/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /w/: Round the lips; raise the back of the tongue.
/ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
/k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.
